summary: Michel Soymié was a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies who studied at INALCO. He held posts at the CNRS (1951–1956), EFEO (ca. 1953–1966), Maison Franco-Japonaise (1957–1960), and EPHE (ca. 1966–1992).

Michel Strickmann specialized in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. Educated at Leiden, EPHE, and Paris Diderot under scholars including Kaltenmark and Vandermeersch, he held posts at UC Berkeley (1978), the University of Bordeaux (ca. 1979–1981), and Wissenschaftskolleg zu Berlin.
Michela Clemente is a scholar of Tibetology who studied under Elena De Rossi Filibeck and Hildegard Diemberger. She has held a post as a Marie Sklodowska Curie Fellow at the University of Cambridge.

Michele Kerbaker specialized in Indology and linguistics, studying at the University of Turin under Flechia and Gorresio. He taught Sanskrit at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" in 1870 and held a professorship at the University of Naples Federico II (ca. 1872–1910).
Michele Martin works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Yale University and held a post at National Taiwan University.

Michelle Spuler is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies who earned her PhD at the University of Queensland. She taught at Colorado College and in the Department of Religious Studies at Victoria University of Wellington (ca. 2002–2004).

Michiel de Vaan specializes in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He completed his doctoral studies under Alexander Lubotsky (ca. 1997–2002) and held a post at Leiden University from ca. 2002 to 2014.

Michihiko Komine is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University (ca. 1964–1974) and served there as an assistant (ca. 1974–1980) and professor (ca. 1990–2015). He has also held posts at Kawasaki Daishi Research Institute and JAES.

Michihiko Yajima is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo. He held posts at the University of Tokyo (attested 1992) and as a professor at Tsurumi Women's University (attested 2003).

Michihiro Ikeda is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He has held positions as an instructor at Setagaya Gakuen High School (attested 1996) and Komazawa Junior College (attested 2005), and as a librarian at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (attested 2005–2006).

Michiko Yusa specializes in religious studies, philosophy, and Japanology. She completed her doctoral studies under Raimon Panikkar at the University of California, Santa Barbara, and served as a professor in the Department of Foreign Languages at Western Washington University (ca. 1983–2020).

Michio Kamikawa was a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied at Ritsumeikan University (ca. 1979–1988) and held a post at Aichi Prefectural University from ca. 1998 to 2021.

Michio Yano is an Indologist and historian of science who studied at Kyoto University and Brown University under Kiyoshi Yabuuchi and David Pingree. He served as a professor in the Faculty of Cultural Studies at Kyoto Sangyo University from 1973 to 2015.

Michitoshi Barada is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Jien Abe and J. R. Joshi. He has held posts at Otani University, the Eastern Institute, and the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute.
Michiya Ito was a graduate student and held posts at Tohoku University, with affiliations attested in 1990 and between 2001 and 2004.

Michiyo Hoshi is a scholar of Tibetology and linguistics. She has held posts as a concurrent researcher at Toyo Bunko (attested 2003) and as a collaborative researcher at the Research Institute for Languages and Cultures of Asia and Africa.
Midori Nishino works in Buddhist studies and Indology. She completed doctoral studies at Taisho University (attested 2006) and subsequently held a post there as a researcher (attested 2010–2015).
Mieko Kajihara is a scholar of Indology who studied under Michael Witzel and completed her PhD at Harvard University in 2002.

Migmar Tsering was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under Khenpo Appey Rinpoche. He held posts at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences, and served as head of Sakya College.
Miguel de Unamuno was a philosopher who studied at Universidad Central from ca. 1880 to 1884. He held a post at the University of Salamanca from ca. 1891 to 1936.
